newsitem.title: USA: US stocks end higher to approach record territory.
newsitem.headline: US stocks end higher to approach record territory.

text.p: U.S. blue chip stocks rallied for a third straight session on Tuesday, propelling the Dow industrials back toward record territory.

The Dow rose 30 points to end unofficially at 7038, less than 30 points off its all-time closing high of 7067.46, set a week ago. Investors again focused on a handful of large-cap stocks, mostly to the exclusion of smaller issues.
"Money is continuing to go to large-cap, quality names," said Guy Truicko, portfolio manager at Unity Management. "They have been and continue to be momentum plays."

International Business Machines Corp was again among the strongest Dow stocks, continuing its rebound from a broad sell-off in technology recently. Minnesota Mining and Manufacturing Co rose 3-1/2 to 90 to lead Dow gainers.

The rally came despite an extremely cautious session in the bond market, which ground to a virtual standstill ahead of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's semi-annual testimony to the U.S. Senate on Wednesday.
Even amid evidence that inflation currently poses little if any threat to the U.S. economy, analysts said Greenspan's testimony, as always, will take center stage.
Recalling the market tumult that followed Greenspan's allusion to "irrational exuberance" during a speech two months ago, Truicko said, "I hope he doesn't decide to elaborate any further on that."
Even so, he noted, "We're up about 10 percent since those comments."

Investor caution ahead of the speech failed to damp enthusiasm for blue chips, which continue to find buyers after every downturn and show little sign of pausing after their torrid run to start the year.

"We continue to fracture the bears and frustrate the sideline money," said Al Goldman, chief market analyst at A.G. Edwards and Sons. "This market for six years now has bent but hasn't broken, and that's how bull markets operate."

Many technology stocks were higher, but the group remained mixed in its performance. Networking leader Cisco Systems Inc dipped 2-1/2 to 56-1/2 after warning that declining capital spending and the strong dollar were eroding sales growth in some of its international markets.
Oil shares also firmed. Chevron Corp gained 1-3/4 to 68 and Texaco Inc rose 2-1/8 to 104-1/8.

Among the session's standouts was recent castaway Centennial Technologies Inc, which rebounded sharply from its recent sell-off. The stock surged 10-1/4 to 14-3/4 before the NYSE halted trading in the shares late in the day.

In an interview, Centennial's interim chief executive told Reuters the company posted record sales last week and said customers were not abandoning the company despite its recent disclosure of accounting irregularities, which will force it to restate results for this year and last.

ClinTrials Research Inc skidded 13-3/4 to 9-1/2 after warning that it expected its first-quarter net income to fall to $0.04 per share from $0.08 last year. The company cited project cancellations for the decline.
